summary: Bora Bora Airport (BOB/NTTB) is located on the motu (small island) of Motu Mute, serving as the main gateway to the world-famous Bora Bora lagoon and its luxury overwater resorts. The airport sits on a narrow strip of land surrounded by turquoise lagoon waters, requiring a short shuttle boat transfer to reach the main island of Vaitape. Despite its modest size, it handles significant international tourist traffic and offers one of the most scenic arrivals in the Pacific.
faqs:
Q: Is there a ferry or boat transfer from Bora Bora Airport to the main island?
A: Yes, a free shuttle boat operated by the airport or your hotel typically ferries passengers across the lagoon to Vaitape on the main island. The crossing takes about 10-15 minutes.

Q: How far is the airport from the resorts on Bora Bora?
A: After the boat shuttle to Vaitape, most resorts are reached by additional boat transfers ranging from 10 to 45 minutes depending on their location on the motu ring surrounding the lagoon.

Q: Are there car rentals available at Bora Bora Airport?
A: No, car rentals are not available at the airport since the main island has limited road infrastructure and most visitors rely on boat transfers arranged through hotels.

Q: Can you walk off the plane directly onto the tarmac?
A: Yes, most flights use outdoor airstairs and passengers walk directly to the small terminal, enjoying immediate views of the lagoon right at the runway edge.
transport_tips: Arrange your resort boat transfer in advance, as the lagoon crossing is the only practical way to reach accommodations. Confirm whether your hotel provides complimentary airport boat pickup or if you need to book independently through Bora Bora Shuttle. Allow extra time for baggage claim, as the small terminal can become congested during peak flight arrivals.
local_tip: Sit on the left side of the aircraft when approaching from Papeete for the best aerial views of Mount Otemanu and the lagoon during landing.
